tests: the exclusion module names no machine identity source

consumesExternalOutput.program: git ls-remote / git commit-tree / git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha>
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: src/exclusion.ts and src/commands/init.ts both spawn git and read its verdicts, so SPAWN_GREP matches them and red-witness rule (f) binds every witness whose members touch them. The cited capture is a REAL forced contention on a bare repository, captured 2026-09-17 with git 2.43.0 and node v26.6.0: it records that git commit-tree exits 128 with `fatal: empty ident name` when no identity is in scope, that the exact-sha --force-with-lease form is ACCEPTED against the value the register holds and REFUSED with `! [rejected] ... (stale info)` against any other, that ls-remote against a path that is not a repository exits 128 while ls-remote for an absent ref exits 0 with empty output, and that the FIRST stderr line of every push here is a push negotiation warning that is byte-identical on the accepted and the refused arms. That last fact is why src/exclusion.ts selects git's own `! [rejected]` marker instead of the first line, and it is the reason a hand-written expectation would have been indistinguishable from a fabricated one (T-003). The named test reads the capture and then reproduces the accept and refuse arms against a live scratch repository. Plan constraint C-2 forbids deriving identity from the running program or the machine, and the criterion names its own check. Member 0 is the forbidden state itself, an environment id built from the running program's identifier; member 1 is the quieter one, a machine name reaching the module through an unrelated constant. They are structurally different because the first changes what the id IS and the second only what the module MENTIONS, and the check has to catch both or it is a comment rather than a guard.
